dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?

Good morning. I would like to inquire about a drainage problem near my residence. Excuse me one moment, I am driving and I am hunting for my keys, the apartment ones, they slid off the seat. Sorry. Hello, are you still there?
I'm here, take your time. Pull over if you need to. What's going on with the drainage?

I am fine, I am at a light. So, there is water ponding at the curb in front of 27 Old Beach Road, on the Easton's Beach side. And there has been no storm. It has been dry for days. It is only meltwater from the snow bank, and it has nowhere to go.
Okay, 27 Old Beach Road. And the water's sitting at the curb, no storm, just melt. Is that right?

That is correct. And then overnight it freezes into black ice across the bottom of the sidewalk and part of the street. I would like to be clear that somebody is going to slip on it. I nearly did this morning, in fact.
Yeah, that's no good. Is it backing up out of a drain, or is there just no drain where it's pooling?

There is a grate, but it appears to be blocked or frozen over. The water does not go in. Instead it is running along the gutter and moving toward my neighbor's garage. It is not inside yet, but it is headed to the driveway apron.

Alright, so the water's heading toward the neighbor's garage. Let me make sure I have this. Grate at the curb in front of 27 Old Beach Road, blocked, meltwater pooling and freezing at night, and running toward the garage next door.
Yes, exactly. Now, I would like to ask whether this is a city drain or a state one. Someone told me that some roads out that way belong to the state, and I do not wish to be sent in circles.
Fair question. Old Beach Road is a city street as far as I know, so the drain at the curb would be ours. If it turns out to be state, we'd pass it along ourselves, you wouldn't have to chase it.
I appreciate that. I would, however, prefer that it be addressed soon. It is a hazard, and I have mentioned it to my landlord, who says it is not his concern.
Understood. I'll put in a work order for a crew to check the grate and clear it. With the freeze-thaw, they may put down some sand or salt too. Do you want a call back when it's been looked at?
Yes, please. My number is 401-555-0173.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-three. Got it. And the name?
Barbara Tillinghast. Tillinghast, T-I-L-L-I-N-G-H-A-S-T.
Thank you, Barbara. I have you down. They'll likely get out there in the next day or two, depending on what else is on the list.
The next day or two. Very well. That means at least one more night of ice, but I understand. Thank you for your help. Oh, I have found my keys. They were in my coat pocket the entire time.
Always the last place. Take care driving, and watch your step out there.
I shall. Goodbye.
